findings.title: Any logged-in user can queue arbitrary DocType inserts that the hourly scheduler commits as Administrator
findings.description: frappe.deferred_insert.deferred_insert is @frappe.whitelist() with no has_permission/only_for check and blindly Redis-RPUSHes attacker-controlled (doctype, records) under insert_queue_for_<doctype>. Hourly scheduler hook frappe.deferred_insert.save_to_db (frappe/hooks.py) runs after frappe.connect(), which always set_user('Administrator'). insert_record then calls Document.insert() under Administrator, so create-permission checks pass for every DocType (and istable DocTypes such as Has Role / DocPerm always return True from has_permission anyway). Designed only for Route History telemetry, but the whitelist accepts any doctype/payload. After insert, frappe.sessions.clear clears the attacker's roles cache so the new System Manager role is effective on the next request.
findings.impact: Website User privilege escalation to System Manager (or arbitrary DocType/DocPerm/Custom DocPerm/Email Account creation) once the hourly scheduler runs, yielding full site takeover.
findings.attack_path:
1. Sign up / authenticate as Website User.
2. POST /api/method/frappe.deferred_insert.deferred_insert with doctype=Has Role and records as a JSON string: [{"doctype":"Has Role","parent":"<attacker_email>","parenttype":"User","parentfield":"roles","role":"System Manager"}].
3. Wait for hourly scheduler event frappe.deferred_insert.save_to_db (hooks.py hourly list). Worker calls frappe.connect() → set_user('Administrator'), then insert_record → doc.insert() as Administrator.
4. POST /api/method/frappe.sessions.clear to clear_user_cache (including roles) for the attacker.
5. Subsequent requests see System Manager via tabHas Role. Alternate payloads: DocPerm/Custom DocPerm granting All write on User, or any other Admin-creatable DocType.
findings.remediation: Remove the public whitelist or hard-allowlist deferred_insert to Route History only. Enforce the caller's create permission on doctype before enqueue, and run save_to_db inserts as the originating user (store user on the queue item) rather than Administrator. Reject istable/child DocTypes unless parent write is authorized.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not on the prompt already-reported list and absent from the 52 stored findings. Distinct from update_document_title (field UPDATE via db.set_value) and from get_data_for_custom_field (read dump): this is unauthorized CREATE executed as Administrator via the scheduler queue. Patching title-write or dump endpoints does not touch deferred_insert.py.
